detail.LT_SUMA: 본 교과목은 파이썬(Python) 프로그래밍의 기초부터 응용까지 학습하는 과목이다. 변수, 자료형, 조건문, 반복문, 함수, 객체지향 프로그래밍 등 핵심 개념을 익히고, 다양한 실습을 통해 문제 해결 능력과 프로그래밍 역량을 배양한다.
detail.LT_PURO:
1. 파이썬 프로그래밍의 기본 문법과 개념을 이해한다.
2. 프로그램 설계 및 구현 능력을 습득한다.
3. 데이터 처리 및 문제 해결을 위한 프로그래밍 기법을 학습한다.
4. 실습과 프로젝트를 통해 실무형 프로그래밍 역량을 강화한다.
detail.ETC:
1. 개인 노트북(Windows, macOS, Linux 가능)
2. Python 개발 환경(Anaconda 또는 VS Code/PyCharm 등)
3. 강의자료 및 실습용 데이터
4. 수업 공지 및 과제 제출을 위한 LMS 접속 환경
detail.LRN_ITGT: 수강생은 모든 과제와 실습을 본인의 노력으로 수행해야 하며, 표절·무단 복제·부정행위를 금지한다. 생성형 AI 및 외부 자료 활용 시에는 교수의 지침을 준수하고 출처를 명확히 밝혀야 한다.
detail.LT_POLY:
1. 출석, 과제, 실습, 시험을 종합적으로 평가한다.
2. 정해진 기한 내에 과제를 제출해야 하며, 지각 제출은 감점될 수 있다.
3. 수업 중 "적극적인 참여"와 실습 수행을 권장한다.
4. 강의자료의 무단 배포 및 공유를 금지한다.

4. 온라인 학습 자료와 과제를 활용한 자기주도 학습을 지원한다.

detail.LT_SUMA: Chemical engineering is a multidisciplinary field that focuses on the economic   production of chemical products through the application of chemical reactions. Beyond   chemistry, it requires a comprehensive understanding of several key areas, including:   Mass/Energy Balance, Reaction Engineering, Fluid Dynamics, Heat and Mass Transfer,   Process Design and Control. This introductory course aims to make these concepts   accessible and easy to understand. It provides a clear understanding of what chemical   engineering entails and is designed to equip students with the fundamental skills   needed to integrate and apply these principles effectively in real-world scenarios.
detail.LT_PURO: To distinguish between chemistry and chemical engineering, and understand the role of   a chemical engineer. To get essential chemical engineering concepts, including unit   conversion, mass balance, energy balance, reaction engineering, fluid mechanics, heat   and mass transfer, process design, and control. To learn how to interpret a given   chemical process from an engineering perspective.
detail.LRN_ITGT: A sincere and proactive attitude is required.
detail.LT_POLY: Some engineering calculators may be required.

detail.LT_SUMA: Students will gain hands-on experience in implementing and testing electronic circuits. They will use measurement equipment to build functional circuits on breadboards with passive and active components while developing practical debugging and troubleshooting skills. The final three weeks of the course will be devoted to a creative design project, where students will design, implement, and present a circuit of their own choice.
detail.LT_PURO: Develop the ability to implement and test basic electronic circuits through hands-on experiments.
detail.LRN_ITGT: Active discussion and collaboration among students are strongly encouraged. However, all reports must be prepared independently. Any plagiarism or unauthorized use of another person’s work without proper citation will be considered academic misconduct and may result in a substantial reduction in grade.
detail.ALL_CNTN:
Week 1: Introduction to the Laboratory Environment

- Voltage and current measurements
- Breadboard usage
- RC transient simulation

Week 2: Kirchhoff’s Laws

- Voltage and current dividers
- Practice with Thévenin’s theorem

Week 3: RLC Circuits

- Reactance and impedance
- Phasor representation of AC signals

Week 4: Operational Amplifiers I

- Inverting and non-inverting amplifiers

Weeks 5–6: Operational Amplifiers II

- Summing amplifier and voltage follower
* Differentiator and integrator
* Comparator

Week 7: Introduction to the Laboratory Environment II

- Basic digital operations, loops, and shift registers
- RC transient experiments

Week 8: Midterm Examination

Week 9: Diodes I

- I–V characteristics
- Light-emitting diodes (LEDs)

Week 10: Diodes II

- Half-wave rectifier
- Full-wave rectifier

Week 11: Transistors I

- BJT characteristic curves
- Early voltage

Week 12: Transistors II

- Common-emitter amplifier
- Emitter follower

Weeks 13–14: Creative Design Project

- Design, implementation, and testing of a student-selected electronic circuit

Week 15: Creative Design Project Presentations

Week 16: Final Examination

detail.LT_SUMA:
이 강의 시리즈에서는 신경세포의 기본 특성부터 뇌의 구조, 감각 시스템 및 관련 질병에 대해 가르칠 것입니다. 이 과정은 뇌과학을 전공으로 선택하고자 하는 학생들과 뇌 관련 연구 주제에 관심이 있는 학생들에게 강력히 추천합니다.
This lecture series will teach from the basic properties of neurons to the structure of the brain, sensory systems, and related diseases. This course is strongly recommended for students who wish to select Brain Sciences as their major, as well as for those interested in brain-related research topics.
detail.LT_PURO:
신경과학 1을 통해 뇌신경세포에 존재하는 분자들의 구조, 기능에 관련된 전반적 지식을 배우며, 신경계에서 작동하는 신경생물학의 일반적 기초를 이해하게 된다. 또한 뇌의 복잡한 구조와 각 부위의 기능에 대해 배우게 되며, 이를 통해 신경과학 2에서 배우게 될 감정과 행동, 인지 등 고차원적 뇌과학을 이해하는 기초를 마련한다. 
In Neuroscience 1, students will learn about the structure and function of molecules present in neural cells, gaining a comprehensive understanding of the general principles of neurobiology that operate within the nervous system. Additionally, they will explore the complex structure of the brain and the functions of its various regions, laying the groundwork for understanding higher-level neuroscience topics such as emotions, behavior, and cognition, which will be covered in Neuroscience 2.

detail.LT_SUMA: 신경과학 II는 『Neuroscience: Exploring the Brain』에서 Part III “The Brain and Behavior”와 Part IV “The Changing Brain”에 해당하는 내용을 중심으로, 뇌가 어떻게 동기·감정·수면·언어·정신질환 등 고차 행동과 정신 기능을 생성하는지 다루는 과목이다.  화학적 신경조절, 동기와 보상, 성과 뇌, 정서·수면·언어·주의·의식의 신경기전, 정신질환의 신경생물학적 기초를 학습한 뒤, 발달과 가소성에 초점을 맞추어 뇌 배선(wiring), 기억 시스템, 학습과 기억의 분자 기전까지를 폭넓게 다룬다.  강의와 더불어 교과서 내 ‘박스(Box)’ 논문을 학생 발표 및 토론 형식으로 진행함으로써, 최신 연구 결과를 비판적으로 읽고 발표·토의 능력을 기르는 것을 목표로 한다.
detail.LT_PURO: 이 과목 수강 후 학생들은 다음을 달성하는 것을 목표로 한다.  1. 화학적 신경조절, 동기·정서·수면·언어·정신질환, 기억과 가소성 등 고등 뇌기능의 기본 개념과 회로 수준 기전을 설명할 수 있다.  2. 신경정신질환 및 인지 기능 장애를 신경회로·분자 수준에서 이해하고, 전임상/임상 연구의 연결 고리를 개략적으로 설명할 수 있다.  3. 교과서의 ‘박스(Box)’ 및 관련 논문을 읽고 핵심 질문·방법·결과·의의를 요약해 발표할 수 있다.  4. 신경과학적 개념을 바탕으로 실제 연구 데이터와 실험 설계를 비판적으로 평가하는 기초 역량을 기른다.

detail.LT_SUMA: Cognitive function refers to the brain's ability to receive and store external information and utilize it to solve problems. It is divided into five major domains: memory, attention, language, executive function, and visuospatial ability. The cognitive functions have been studied through various methods, including observational studies on healthy individuals and patients, as well as animal studies. The knowledge accumulated through these studies is being applied to various cutting-edge fields, such as brain imaging processing and brain-computer interfaces. In this course, you will learn the various elements that constitute human cognitive function and the regions of the brain that process each element.인지기능은 외부의 정보를 받아들이고 저장하며, 이를 활용하여 문제를 해결하는 두뇌 고유의 기능을 말하며, 기억력, 집중력, 언어능력, 실행기능, 시공간능력의 5대 영역으로 나누어진다. 두뇌의 인지기능은 정상인 및 환자를 대상으로 한 관찰연구 및 동물실험연구 등의 다양한 방법을 통해 연구되어 왔으며, 지금까지의 연구를 통해 축적된 지식은 뇌영상처리 및 두뇌-컴퓨터 인터페이스와 같은 다양한 첨단의 분야에 응용되고 있다. 본 과목에서는 인간의 인지기능을 구성하는 다양한 요소와, 각 요소를 처리하는 두뇌의 영역에 대해 공부할 것이다.
detail.LT_PURO:
Upon completion of this course, students will achieve the following:
1. Be able to explain the gross and microscopic anatomical structures and functions that constitute the nervous system.
2. Be able to discuss the classical and cutting-edge methods and indications of research in cognitive neuroscience. 
3. Define the various elements constituting cognitive functions (perception, concentration, learning/memory, cognitive function, language) and explain the neural circuits that perform these functions.
4. Define other functions performed in the human brain (sleep/wake, emotion, social interaction) and explain the neural circuits that perform these functions.

목표: 본 과목을 이수한 후에는 다음과 같은 사항을 달성해야 한다.

3주차:Weeks 2 and 3 (September 2, 2026 – September 7, 2026, Research methods):- Understand the indications and limitations of various techniques used in human neuroscience research.- Understand the indications, advantages and disadvantages of techniques used in animal-based neuroscience research.- Be able to select the most suitable technique among various experimental methods to suit the research objectives.- 사람 대상의 신경과학의 연구에 사용되는 다양한 기법들의 적응증 및 한계점에 대해 이해해야 한다.- 동물실험 기반의 신경과학의 연구에 사용되는 기법들의 적응증 및 장단점에 대해 이해해야 한다.- 연구의 목적에 맞게, 다양한 실험기법 중 가장 적합한 기법을 선택할 수 있어야 한다.

detail.LT_SUMA:
This course explores the molecular, cellular, and circuitry mechanisms that underlie the function of the mammalian nervous system, with special emphasis on the membrane potential, electrical signaling and synaptic organization.       
This course will include:    - Surveying the molecular and cellular mechanisms of neuronal communication.    - Coversion channels in excitable membrane, synaptic transmission, and synaptic plasticity.    - Correlation of the properties of ion channels and synaptic transmission with their physiological function such as learning and memory.    - Discussion of the organizational principles for the formation of functional neural networks at synaptic and cellular levels.
detail.LT_PURO: This class aims to learn basic information about neurobiology of physiological processes or using neurophysiological techniques to understand molecular, cellular, systems or behavioral neuroscience, from model organisms to human subjects.

detail.LT_SUMA: This course explores the relationship between biological and artificial intelligence through direct comparison. In the first half of the semester, students study five major comparison components: representation, learning rules, credit assignment, action selection and control, and efficiency/hardware. In the second half, students gain hands-on experience with spiking neural networks using snnTorch. In the final part, students critically evaluate review literature in neuroscience-inspired AI through solo or group presentations.
detail.LT_PURO:
- Explain major computational principles in biological and artificial intelligence
- Compare biological and artificial representations of information
- Distinguish local biological plasticity rules from AI optimization methods
- Describe spatial and temporal credit assignment problems
- Explain reinforcement learning concepts in relation to dopamine and basal ganglia circuits
- Implement basic spiking neural network models using snnTorch
- Critically analyze review literature in neuroscience-inspired AI
- Evaluate the strengths and limits of neuroscience–AI analogies
detail.ETC:
- Kandel et al., Principles of Neural Science (Fifth Edition)
- Sutton and Barto, Reinforcement Learning (Second Edition)
- https://snntorch.readthedocs.io/en/latest/index.html

detail.LT_SUMA: The concepts of limit, derivative, and integral of single-variable functions are extended to multivariate functions and their applications. And this course deals with the basic concepts of 3 by 3 matrices, solving simultaneous ordinary differential equations using matrices, defining multiple integrals, understanding the physics of vector field integration, learning theories such as Stokes' theorem and divergence theorem, and learning Maxwell's equations. Also deals with how to derive fluid dynamics equations by applying the integral theorems.
detail.LT_PURO: Understand the concepts of differentiation and integration of multi-variable functions

detail.LT_SUMA: In this course we will cover concepts and applications of differentiation and integration of real multivariable functions and vector analysis. Topics will include: elements of Euclidean geometry, limits and continuity of multivariable functions, differentiability, gradients and directional derivatives, higher derivatives, maxima and minima, vector fields, divergence and curl, multiple integrals, path and surface integrals, Green, Stokes and Gauss theorems.

detail.LT_SUMA: Differential equations represent a fundamental mathematical tool used by the whole of science to model physical phenomena: they express how a certain quantity of interest is related to its derivatives. Solutions to such problems are given by differentiable functions, which can be used to provide estimates and predict the evolution of the physical system one is studying. In this course students will learn how to solve several types of ordinary differential equations and also how to investigate and interpret the results.
detail.LT_PURO: Students are expected to critically apply the different methods of solution of differential equations presented in the course and to able to interpret and effectively investigate the solutions obtained, both numerically and qualitatively.
detail.ETC: Lecture notes and the recordings of the lectures will be made available on LMS.

In particular, not attending either the midterm or the final will result in a failing grade. Exceptions to this general rule will be granted on a case-by-case basis at the discretion of the instructor.   Make-up exams will be granted only in exceptional cases, following the submission of appropriate documentation explaining the circumstances.  Cheating and plagiarism will not be tolerated and, if discovered, will lead to failing the entire course. This also applies to students who knowingly allow their work to be copied.
detail.LSN_MTHD: The course will mainly consists of frontal lectures, with some in-class opportunities for the students to test their understanding with some exercises. Homework exercises will be provided to prepare the students for the biweekly quizzes.

detail.LT_SUMA: This course introduces the fundamental concepts of electromagnetism in an accessible and intuitive manner. Topics include electric forces and fields, electric potential, electric current, resistance, and basic electrical circuits. Students will explore magnetic fields, magnetic forces, and electromagnetic induction, with emphasis on practical applications. The course concludes with an introduction to electromagnetic waves, highlighting their properties, behavior, and role in the transmission of energy.
detail.LT_PURO:
By the end of the course, students will be able to:
- Apply vector analysis techniques to problems in electromagnetism
- Explain key principles of electrostatic and magnetostatic fields
- Demonstrate problem-solving skills in various electromagnetic contexts
- Build a strong foundation for further study and practical applications in electromagnetic theory and engineering

Academic dishonesty includes, but is not limited to: violating clearly stated rules for taking an exam or completing an assignment; plagiarism (including material from sources without a citation and quotation marks around any borrowed words); claiming another’s work or a modification of another’s work as one’s own; buying or attempting to buy papers or projects for a course; fabricating information or citations.

Late submissions will result in point deductions that may affect your final grade. If you anticipate a conflict with a due date or encounter difficulties with an assignment, you must plan ahead and notify the instructor in advance. This will allow us to discuss the situation and, if appropriate, make alternative arrangements.

detail.LT_SUMA: This course introduces the fundamental concepts of electromagnetism in an accessible and intuitive manner. Topics include electric forces and fields, electric potential, electric current, resistance, and basic electrical circuits. Students will explore magnetic fields, magnetic forces, and electromagnetic induction, with emphasis on practical applications. The course concludes with an introduction to electromagnetic waves, highlighting their properties, behavior, and role in the transmission of energy.
detail.LT_PURO:
By the end of the course, students will be able to:
- Apply vector analysis techniques to problems in electromagnetism
- Explain key principles of electrostatic and magnetostatic fields
- Demonstrate problem-solving skills in various electromagnetic contexts
- Build a strong foundation for further study and practical applications in electromagnetic theory and engineering

detail.LT_SUMA: While classical mechanics deals with the motion of mass-bearing particles, electromagnetism broadly covers the motion of charged particles and systems of particles. You will learn about electric fields created by stationary charges, magnetic fields created by charges moving at a constant velocity, and electromagnetic waves created by accelerating charges. The course addresses the motion of charges and magnetic moments within these fields, as well as the properties of elements that make up electric circuits. To understand light, the ray model, wave model, and photon model of light will be examined, alongside topics such as reflection, refraction, interference, diffraction, polarization, and the photoelectric effect.
detail.LT_PURO: Understand the basic concepts of charges, electric fields generated by charges, and magnetic fields and electromagnetic waves generated by moving charges. Comprehend the characteristics of light as a type of electromagnetic wave, including reflection, refraction, interference, diffraction, and polarization. Additionally, study basic circuits by understanding the movement of charges.

detail.LT_SUMA: 물리학은 실험과학이다. 실험을 통해서 확인되지 않는 지식은 과학지식이라고 하기 어렵다. 자신이 수행한 실험을 통해 일반물리II 강의를 통해서 배운 지식의 진위를 시험해 보자. 실험 과정 하나하나를 점검해 가면서 자신의 실험과정과 결과에 대해 과학적으로 설명할 수 있어야 한다. 실험을 하고 그것을 통해 과학지식을 확인하는 과정은 물리 뿐만 아니라 모든 실험 과학에서 적용할 수 있다. 실험결과와 여러분이 배운 이론에 바탕 한 계산 값이 맞지 않을 수 있다. 여기에서 새롭고 재미있는 과학이 시작된다. 전자기학 및 광학과 관련된 실험을 통하여 물리 현상을 이해해 본다.

detail.LT_SUMA: 물리학은 실험과학이다. 실험을 통해서 확인되지 않는 지식은 과학지식이라고 하기 어렵다. 자신이 수행한 실험을 통해 일반물리II 강의를 통해서 배운 지식의 진위를 시험해 보자. 실험 과정 하나하나를 점검해 가면서 자신의 실험과정과 결과에 대해 과학적으로 설명할 수 있어야 한다. 실험을 하고 그것을 통해 과학지식을 확인하는 과정은 물리 뿐만 아니라 모든 실험 과학에서 적용할 수 있다. 실험결과와 여러분이 배운 이론에 바탕 한 계산 값이 맞지 않을 수 있다. 여기에서 새롭고 재미있는 과학이 시작된다. 전자기학 및 광학과 관련된 실험을 통하여 물리 현상을 이해해 본다.
detail.LT_PURO: 일반물리II 에서 배우는 전자기 현상과 광학에 대한 기본원리와 법칙들을 실험을 통해 직접 확인해보고 이론과 비교분석함으로써 기초 개념에 대한 이해를 명확히 한다.  조별 실험을 통하여 공동 학습과 탐구 방법을 익힌다.  실험보고서 작성을 통하여 실험 결과의 정리 및 해석 방법을 익힌다.
detail.LRN_ITGT: 실험보고서 작성시 참고 인용 표시 명확하게 한다.
detail.LT_POLY: 실험에 적극적으로 참여한다. 토론에 적극적으로 참여한다. 개인 위생 및 보건 관련 의무 사항을 준수한다.
detail.LSN_MTHD: 해당수업 주제 관련 이론을 사전에 조사하고, 수업 시작시 퀴즈를 실시한다. / 조별로 지정 주제 실험을 수행하고(실험노트 작성) 기한 내에 실험보고서를 제출한다. / 조별로 창의실험을 수행하고 결과를 발표한다.

detail.LT_SUMA: This course introduces experimental topics in electricity, magnetism, and optics. Students investigate electrostatic and magnetostatic phenomena, DC and AC circuits, and the properties of light as an electromagnetic wave. Through hands-on experiments and discussions, they develop an understanding of fundamental electromagnetic principles and their applications. The course culminates in creative team projects in which students design and conduct experiments on self-selected topics to explore innovative applications of electromagnetism.
detail.LT_PURO:
To gain practical insight into the fundamental concepts of electromagnetism underlying electrical engineering and optics through laboratory experiments.
To develop competence in collecting and analyzing experimental data to identify the physical principles governing observed phenomena.
To enhance the ability to design experiments, interpret results, and communicate scientific work effectively through written reports and presentations.
detail.LRN_ITGT: Students are expected to maintain academic integrity by clearly citing and properly acknowledging all references and sources used in the preparation of laboratory reports.
detail.LT_POLY:
Students are expected to actively participate in all laboratory activities.
Students are expected to actively engage in discussions and contribute to the exchange of ideas.
Students must comply with all requirements and guidelines related to personal hygiene and health.
detail.LSN_MTHD:
Students are expected to review the theoretical background related to each experiment in advance, and a quiz will be administered at the beginning of class.
Students work in teams to conduct assigned experiments, maintain laboratory notebooks, and submit laboratory reports within three days of completing the experiments.
Students collaborate in teams to design and carry out creative experiments and present their results to the class.

detail.LT_SUMA:
화학은 물질의 정체와 변환을 연구하는 자연과학의 핵심 분야로, 원자와 분자를 이용하여 새로운 화합물을 합성하며 다양한 화학 반응의 특성을 연구하는 분야이다. 학문적으로는 자연과 인간의 생명 현상을 이해하고 더 나은 삶을 위한 관련 첨단과학을 선도하며 산업적으로는 인류의 삶에 필요한 다양한 소재와 에너지를 공급해주고 있다. 실험으로 얻어진 결과와 이론적으로 예측된 값을 비교하여 화학적 사고확장을 유도한다.
(Chemistry is a core field of natural science that studies the identity and transformation of matter, synthesizing new compounds using atoms and molecules, and studying the properties of various chemical reactions. Academically, it understands the phenomena of nature and human life, leads the related advanced science for a better life, and provides various materials and energy necessary for human life industrially. By comparing the experimental results with the theoretically predicted values, it induces the expansion of chemical thinking.)
detail.LT_PURO:
일반화학실험은 일반화학에서 배운 내용들을 직접 실험을 통하여 검증하여 내용에 대한 단순한 습득이 아니라 실험 전 보고서의 작성을 통해 미리 실험에 대한 계획을 세우고, 조원들과 협력하여 실험을 진행하며, 실험 후 결과 보고서의 작성을 통해 실험 결과의 이해와 실험 과정의 문제성을 되짚어 사고할 수 있다.
(In general chemical experiments, it is possible to review the problems of the experimental process and understand the results of the experiment through the preparation of a pre-experiment report rather than simply acquiring the contents through experiments.)
detail.LRN_ITGT:
실험 전 미리 실험에 대한 정보와 주의점을 확인하고 얻어진 결과로 정직하게 결론을 도출한다. 항상 교우들과 협동하여 실험에 임한다. 실험에 임할 때는 항상 주의하여 사고가 나지 않게 미연에 방지한다.
(Before the experiment, check the information and precautions of the experiment in advance and draw conclusions honestly from the obtained results. Always work with your classmates to experiment. Always be careful when engaging in an experiment to prevent accidents.)
detail.LT_POLY:
사전 보고서를 통해 실험 전 내용을 숙지하고 조별로 실험하며 얻어진 결과는 함께 논의 하되 보고서는 개별 제출한다. 
(Through a preliminary report, familiarize yourself with the pre-experiment contents and discuss the results obtained by experimenting in groups together, but submit the report individually.)

화학은 물질의 정체와 변환을 연구하는 자연과학의 핵심 분야로, 원자와 분자를 이용하여 새로운 화합물을 합성하며 다양한 화학 반응의 특성을 연구하는 분야이다. 학문적으로는 자연과 인간의 생명 현상을 이해하고 더 나은 삶을 위한 관련 첨단과학을 선도하며 산업적으로는 인류의 삶에 필요한 다양한 소재와 에너지를 공급해주고 있다. 실험으로 얻어진 결과와 이론적으로 예측된 값을 비교하여 화학적 사고확장을 유도한다.
(Chemistry is a core field of natural science that studies the identity and transformation of matter, synthesizing new compounds using atoms and molecules, and studying the properties of various chemical reactions. Academically, it understands the phenomena of nature and human life, leads the related advanced science for a better life, and provides various materials and energy necessary for human life industrially. By comparing the experimental results with the theoretically predicted values, it induces the expansion of chemical thinking.)
detail.LT_PURO:
일반화학실험은 일반화학에서 배운 내용들을 직접 실험을 통하여 검증하여 내용에 대한 단순한 습득이 아니라 실험 전 보고서의 작성을 통해 미리 실험에 대한 계획을 세우고, 조원들과 협력하여 실험을 진행하며, 실험 후 결과 보고서의 작성을 통해 실험 결과의 이해와 실험 과정의 문제성을 되짚어 사고할 수 있다.
(In general chemical experiments, it is possible to review the problems of the experimental process and understand the results of the experiment through the preparation of a pre-experiment report rather than simply acquiring the contents through experiments.)
detail.LRN_ITGT:
실험 전 미리 실험에 대한 정보와 주의점을 확인하고 얻어진 결과로 정직하게 결론을 도출한다. 항상 교우들과 협동하여 실험에 임한다. 실험에 임할 때는 항상 주의하여 사고가 나지 않게 미연에 방지한다.
(Before the experiment, check the information and precautions of the experiment in advance and draw conclusions honestly from the obtained results. Always work with your classmates to experiment. Always be careful when engaging in an experiment to prevent accidents.)
detail.LT_POLY:
사전 보고서를 통해 실험 전 내용을 숙지하고 조별로 실험하며 얻어진 결과는 함께 논의 하되 보고서는 개별 제출한다. 
(Through a preliminary report, familiarize yourself with the pre-experiment contents and discuss the results obtained by experimenting in groups together, but submit the report individually.)

Throughout the course, students will perform prearranged experimental procedures, work collaboratively with classmates, and accurately collect and analyze experimental data. Emphasis is placed on proper laboratory practices and safety awareness to minimize accidents and maintain a safe learning environment.

detail.LT_SUMA: This laboratory course introduces students to fundamental techniques and experimental approaches in biology, reinforcing core concepts through hands-on investigation. Students will conduct experiments in areas such as microscopy, cell biology, enzyme activity, genetics, and molecular biology. Emphasis is placed on developing skills in hypothesis formulation, experimental design, data collection and analysis, and scientific communication. The course complements the associated lecture by providing experiential learning opportunities that highlight the process of scientific inquiry and the application of biological principles in real-world contexts.
detail.LT_PURO: This course aims to develop students’ practical skills in experimental biology, including accurate use of laboratory equipment, microscopy, and basic techniques in molecular and cellular biology. Students will learn to formulate testable hypotheses, design and carry out experiments, record observations, analyze quantitative and qualitative data, and interpret results in the context of core biological concepts. The course also emphasizes clear and precise scientific communication through written lab reports and collaborative discussions.

detail.LT_SUMA: This course provides an introduction to fundamental biological principles, emphasizing the molecular and cellular basis of life, genetics, evolution, and the structure-function relationships in living organisms. Topics include the chemistry of life, cell structure and function, metabolism, DNA replication and expression, Mendelian and molecular genetics, and evolutionary processes. The course is designed for students pursuing studies in life sciences, medicine, neuroscience or related fields and provides the foundational knowledge required for advanced coursework in biology.
detail.LT_PURO: This course aims to provide students with a foundational understanding of general biology by exploring the chemical basis of life, cell structure and function, energy metabolism, molecular genetics, and evolution. Students will learn to describe key biological molecules and processes, explain genetic inheritance and gene expression, and analyze the mechanisms driving evolutionary change. Emphasis is placed on developing scientific reasoning skills, interpreting experimental data, and understanding how molecular and cellular processes underlie organismal biology.

detail.LT_SUMA: This course provides an integrated introduction to animal and plant biology, evolution, and ecology. Students will learn how animals maintain homeostasis through coordinated physiological systems, how plants grow, reproduce, and respond to their environment, and how evolutionary processes generate biological diversity. The course also examines ecological interactions at the levels of populations, communities, and ecosystems. Emphasis is placed on understanding fundamental biological principles and applying them to real-world biological phenomena.
detail.LT_PURO: The primary objective of this course is to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of the fundamental principles of animal and plant biology, evolution, and ecology. Students will develop an understanding of how animal physiological systems function to maintain homeostasis, how plants grow, reproduce, and respond to environmental cues, and how evolutionary processes generate and shape biological diversity. The course also aims to introduce the ecological interactions that occur among organisms and between organisms and their environment across multiple levels of biological organization. Through the integration of concepts from physiology, development, evolution, and ecology, students will strengthen their ability to think critically about biological systems and apply scientific reasoning to the analysis of biological phenomena.

detail.LT_SUMA: General Chemistry I course introduces foundational concepts in chemistry, focusing on the structure and properties of matter. Students will explore atomic theory, periodic trends, chemical bonding, molecular geometry, and the principles governing chemical reactions and stoichiometry. The course also covers gases, liquids, solids, and intermolecular forces, providing a solid foundation in fundamental chemistry concepts.
detail.LT_PURO: This course is designed to introduce students to the fundamental principles of chemistry. Students will develop a solid understanding of atomic structure, chemical bonding, stoichiometry, and the properties of gases, liquids, and solids. Emphasis is placed on developing quantitative problem-solving skills and applying chemical concepts to real-world phenomena, as well as preparing students for more advanced studies in science and engineering.

detail.LT_SUMA: General Chemistry II builds upon the fundamental principles introduced in General Chemistry I by examining the behavior of chemical systems in greater depth. Students will explore the properties of solutions, chemical kinetics, chemical equilibrium, acid-base equilibria, thermodynamics, electrochemistry, nuclear chemistry, and the chemistry of nonmetals and transition metals. The course emphasizes the factors that govern chemical reactions, energy transformations, and equilibrium processes, while highlighting applications in environmental, industrial, biological, and technological contexts.

detail.LT_SUMA: This course provides an introduction to probability and statistical inference with an emphasis on fundamental concepts and their mathematical foundations. Topics include probability models, random variables and their distributions, joint and conditional distributions, sampling distributions, estimation, hypothesis testing, and simple linear regression. The course integrates theoretical development with illustrative examples and applications to data.
detail.LT_PURO: By the end of the course, students should be able to formulate problems in probabilistic terms, apply standard methods of estimation and hypothesis testing, and draw appropriate conclusions from data. The course also aims to strengthen quantitative reasoning and the clear communication of statistical results.
detail.ETC: Students are expected to have successfully completed Multivariable Calculus (BS101) or an equivalent course. Familiarity with basic calculus, algebraic manipulation, and mathematical notation is expected. Students must have regular access to a laptop computer for assignments and computational demonstrations as required.
detail.LRN_ITGT: Cheating and plagiarism are serious offenses and will not be tolerated. Any student caught plagiarizing or cheating will automatically fail the course. This also applies to students who knowingly allow their work to be copied.
detail.LT_POLY: Attendance of the midterm and final exams are mandatory (absence in either exam will result in a failing grade). Make-up exams might be granted upon request, in a case-by-case basis and with appropriate documentation explaining each circumstance.

detail.LT_SUMA:
학부과정에서 미적분학과 함께 가장 중요하고도 흥미롭고, 응용성에서는 오히려 미적분학보다 더 광범위한 선형대수의 주요 개념을 배웁니다. 먼저, 자연현상 속에 널리 퍼져 있는 ‘선형성(Linearity)’이라는 것들을 관찰하고, 그것이 어떻게 수학적으로 정리되고 표현되어 질 수 있는지를 이해합니다. 그리고 이 선형성을 담고 있는 대상(object) 그리 고 그 대상간의 사상(mapping)이 다변수미적분학 시간에 학습한 ‘행렬(matrix)’로 나타날 수 있음을 자연스레 이해한 뒤 행렬에 대해 흥미로운 여러가지 문제들을 생각합니다. 이렇게 학습한 내용을 바탕으로 처음 시작했던 자연과학과 공학, 경제학 등에서 등장하는 여러 문제들에 선형대수를 이용한 응용을 학습하는 것이 이 과목의 내용이자 목표입니다.    

In the course, you will learn the main concepts of linear algebra, which is the most important and interesting course along with calculus, but is in fact broader than calculus in applications. First of all, we consider ‘Linearity’, which is widespread in sciences and engineering, and understand how it can be organized and expressed mathematically. And after naturally understanding that the object containing this linearity and the mapping between the objects can be represented as a 'matrix' learned in multivariable calculus class, we started to solve various interesting problems about matrices. I think. Based on what you have learned in this way, the content and goal of this course is to learn the application of linear algebra to various problems that appear in natural sciences, engineering, and economics, which you first started with.
detail.LT_PURO:
해당과목에 대한 특별한 선수과목은 없습니다. 다변수미적분학에서 배운 행렬과 연립일차방정식에 대한 기본적인 이해만 있으면 가능합니다 (물론 이 부분도 강의 초반부에 복습할 예정입니다). 본 수업은 이렇게 흥미롭고 중요한 선형대수의 원리적인 측면을 더 깊이 이해하고 다양한 연립일차방정식의 해법과 응용에 관한 필요한 기본적인 계산을 직접 또는 소프트웨어를 이용해 수행할 수 있는 것을 목표로 합니다.     

The successful student will know how to solve system of linear equations, basic matrix arithmetics and basic notions linear algebra such as linearity, vector spaces, linear mapping, basis, dimensions. The student understands the statements and ideas of proof of many important theorems in the course. He or she also will be able to do relevant calculations for typical problems related to these topics.

detail.LT_SUMA: The following contents are introduced (1) Interpretation of heat transfer, (2) Molecular basis of diffusion in gas, liquid, polymer, and solid, (3) Condition description of diffusion in binary and multi-component mixtures with and without chemical reactions.
detail.LT_PURO: ● Analysis of chemical engineering operations involving heat. ● Understanding heat transfer, especially in the chemical process. ● Understanding mathematical models for heat and mass transfer. ● Applying mathematical models on real heat and mass transfer.

detail.LT_SUMA: Fundamental principles of inorganic chemistry such as atomic structure, molecular orbital theory, molecular symmetry, and coordination chemistry related to chemical bonding and molecular geometry will be discussed. A study of the energetics of the bonding and reactions of inorganic compounds will be included. Emphasis will be placed on the periodicity of the chemical and physical properties of the elements. The course also covers key concepts related to the chemistry of the elements such as effective nuclear charge, lattice energy, and electron density.
detail.LT_PURO:
1.To understand the fundamental concepts of inorganic chemistry. 
2.To develop the ability to apply chemical principles to explain and predict the properties and reactivity of inorganic compounds.
3.To develop critical thinking and problem-solving skills in chemistry.

detail.LT_SUMA: This course provides a systematic introduction to the mathematical foundations of computer science. Building on mathematical preliminaries such as set theory, logic, and induction, the course covers three core topics. First, students study finite automata, regular expressions, and the properties of regular languages to understand the simplest computational models. Second, context-free languages and pushdown automata are explored to describe the grammatical structure of programming languages. Third, students examine the origins of computer science and study Turing machines — the theoretical model underlying modern computers — in both standard and extended forms, gaining insight into the nature of computability, undecidability (including the Halting Problem), and computational complexity through P, NP, and NP-completeness theory.
detail.LT_PURO:
Upon completion of this course, students will be able to:
1. Understand and explain the mathematical models of computation: finite automata, pushdown automata, and Turing machines.
2. Analyze the properties of regular and context-free languages, and apply the Pumping Lemma to classify formal languages.
3. Understand computability and undecidability through the lens of Turing machines, and prove representative undecidable problems such as the Halting Problem.
4. Understand P, NP, and NP-completeness, and classify problems from the perspective of computational complexity.
5. Develop rigorous mathematical reasoning and proof-writing skills applicable across all areas of computer science.

detail.LSN_MTHD:
➀강의, ➁발표, ➂토론/토의, 
교과목의 특성 상 집중적인 강의를 주로 하되 수강생과의 대화와 토론이 매우 중요할 것임. 강의 중 질문을 하는 경우, 부담 없이 적극적으로 토론에 참여함을 요망함.
detail.SCHETCHUL:
1주차:강의/교수 소개, 글로벌 기술전쟁과 기업가 정신
2주차:글로벌 기술전쟁과 트럼프의 “MAGA” 정책
3주차:NASDAQ Big Tech 기업들
4주차:실리콘밸리, what it is, what it is not, 기업가와 기업가정신 
5주차:혁신의 이해, 석기에서 AI까지 만들어낸 인간의 생각
6주차:도구 발전은 “새로운 착상”의 역사“새로운 착상”의 원천 : 수렴적 사고와 발산적 사고의 콜라보
7주차:도구를 만드는 도구 – 과학과 기술   Science Push vs. Technology Push   과학은 혁명적(revolution)으로 변화하지만 기술은 진화(evolution)한다.   기술 패러다임과 기술 궤적(Technological Trajectories) 
8주차:Midterm Exam.
9주차:경영의 세계 : 경영의 일반론
10주차:혁신이란 무엇인가? 경영과 혁신, 혁신의 촉발 요인
11주차:혁신의 문화, 혁신의 유형, Big Bang Innovation, 신속결합혁신
12주차:기술경영(MOT) 기초 
13주차:기술경영(MOT) 기초 
14주차:기술경영(MOT) 기초 
15주차:지속가능한 기업가 혁신(Sustainable Entrepreneurship)
16주차:Final Exam.  위 일정은 강의 진행과정에서 변경될 수 있음을 유의해야 함

detail.LT_SUMA: This course is designed to help students develop the English skills needed for academic and professional purposes. It aims to provide students with an opportunity to familiarize themselves with the use of English in a variety of stimulating topics. Students will work towards improving their ability to work with the de facto language of international academia: English.
detail.LT_PURO:
By the end of this course, students will learn and be able to:
Find and critically evaluate sources in English.
Understand and critically summarize articles in English.
Synthesize multiple sources to support or refute a claim or argument.
Formally communicate academic research and writing. 
Use language and organizational skills for writing an evidence-based persuasive essay.
Behavior and Performance Objectives:
By the end of this course, students will be able to:
Actively reflect on their learning progress, evaluate their strengths and weaknesses in English, and take corrective action as required.
Think critically when responding to texts and developing their own thoughts and opinions in both English and their native language.
Effectively work in partnership with others to achieve collective goals through working as a member of a small group to complete assessments and tasks.
Communicate their thoughts and opinions to others more clearly and completely in English and respond to others’ opinions thoughtfully and appropriately for international communication.
Present the process and results of resource evaluations and summarizations. 
Write an evidence-based persuasive essay using relevant information and logic that follows  academic writing standards.
detail.LRN_ITGT:
Academic dishonesty in any form will not be tolerated. Violations of these rules will result in a record of the violation being placed in your file. You may also receive a failing grade for the course. Confirmation of such incidents can also result in expulsion from the university.
Academic Dishonesty includes:
Unauthorized assistance: Using unauthorized materials, information, or study aids in any academic exercise (unless specifically authorized by your professor).
Presenting material (through written, visual, electronic, or oral means) which has not been studied or learned, but rather was obtained through someone else’s efforts and used as part of an examination, course assignment, or project.  
Falsifying or misrepresenting your academic work.
Plagiarism: In which another’s work or ideas are used without indication of the source, thereby conveying the impression that such work is the student’s own. (go to http://www.plagiarism.org/ or https://www.copykiller.co.kr/notice to get more information on plagiarism and how to avoid it)
Multiple Submissions: Submitting the same work for credit more than once without the express permission of the professor. 
Any student who knowingly helps another student violate these academic behavior standards is also in violation of the standards.
detail.LT_POLY:
Attendance Policy
All classes are mandatory and must be attended. If you are unable to attend class, you must inform your professor at least 24 hours prior to your intended absence. If you have a reasonable excuse for your absence you will be given an excused absence. An excused absence does not negatively affect your final grade, however repeated absences (excused or not) may result in a warning from your professor, after which any further absences may lead to being awarded a failing or incomplete grade in the course.
If you miss class due to ill-health, provide a medical certificate to your professor on the first class meeting after your return to receive your excused absence. If you are absent without a reasonable excuse, you will be marked absent from the class meeting. If you are marked absent 4 or more times during the semester you will receive a failing grade for the course.
Please arrive on time for all class meetings. Three late arrivals will result in being marked as an unexcused absence. Arriving more than 20 minutes after the start of class will automatically be marked as an unexcused absence.
Late Work Policy
There are no make-ups for work completed in class, such as group work or presentations. Any work not completed during class time must be finished and turned in by the due date set by your professor.
If you are absent (even if you have a reasonable excuse), it is your responsibility to find out what work was assigned during the classes you missed and to complete that work by the due date. Failure to submit work by the due date is unacceptable, and the work will not receive any feedback.
Group Work Policy
Everyone must take part in group projects. For daily work throughout the semester, you will be assigned to a group. All members of a group will receive the same score. In other words, the assignment is given 1 score, and everyone in the group receives it. For larger assignments and projects, you may work in groups but be assessed individually.
Student/Professor Communication
If you have a question regarding the course administration or course content you should:
Ask your professor during or after class. Because it is common for many students to have the same questions, asking in class allows every student to get the answer at the same time.
Ask your professor via email if you have a private question.
Your professor will designate time each week specifically for helping students.
Your professor will post an appointment sheet on or near their office door. To make an appointment, sign up for the time you wish to visit.
Alternatively, you can send an email to your professor to make an appointment. 
Outside of office hours, your professor may be busy attending to other duties, so they may not be available to meet.

detail.LT_POLY: Professionalism Policy  Per university policy and classroom etiquette, mobile phones and similar devices must be silenced during all classroom sessions. Also, the use of Kakao Talk or similar instant messaging applications is limited to communication or sharing of documents with partners in class. Those not following these rules will be warned, may receive participation credit deductions, be marked as absent, or be asked to leave the classroom to avoid disrupting the learning environment. Students who habitually disturb the class may receive a warning, and ultimately could receive a failing grade. However, directly copying and pasting Machine Translator output is prohibited. Furthermore, copying and pasting Machine Translated or AI Generated content may also result in accidental plagiarism, poor/incorrect word choice, or other problems that may result in point deductions.

detail.LT_SUMA: This course is designed to help students develop the English skills needed for academic and professional purposes. It aims to provide students with an opportunity to familiarize themselves with the use of English in a variety of stimulating topics. Students will work towards improving their ability to work with the de facto language of international academia: English.
detail.LT_PURO: Course Objectives  Language Objectives:  By the end of this course, students will learn and be able to:  ⬥Find and critically evaluate sources in English.  ⬥Understand and critically summarize articles in English.  ⬥Synthesize multiple sources to support or refute a claim or argument.  ⬥Formally communicate academic research and writing.   ⬥Use language and organizational skills for writing an evidence-based persuasive essay.  Behavior and Performance Objectives:  By the end of this course, students will be able to:  ⬥Actively reflect on their learning progress, evaluate their strengths and weaknesses in English, and take corrective action as required.  ⬥Think critically when responding to texts and developing their own thoughts and opinions in both English and their native language.  ⬥Effectively work in partnership with others to achieve collective goals through working as a member of a small group to complete assessments and tasks.  ⬥Communicate their thoughts and opinions to others more clearly and completely in English and respond to others’ opinions thoughtfully and appropriately for international communication.  ⬥Present the process and results of resource evaluations and summarizations.   ⬥Write an evidence-based persuasive essay using relevant information and logic that follows  academic writing standards.
detail.LRN_ITGT: Academic Conduct Policy  Academic dishonesty in any form will not be tolerated. Violations of these rules will result in a record of the violation being placed in your file. You may also receive a failing grade for the course. Confirmation of such incidents can also result in expulsion from the university.  Academic Dishonesty includes:  ⬥Unauthorized assistance: Using unauthorized materials, information, or study aids in any academic exercise (unless specifically authorized by your professor).  ⬥Presenting material (through written, visual, electronic, or oral means) which has not been studied or learned, but rather was obtained through someone else’s efforts and used as part of an examination, course assignment, or project.    ⬥Falsifying or misrepresenting your academic work.  ⬥Plagiarism: In which another’s work or ideas are used without indication of the source, thereby conveying the impression that such work is the student’s own. (go to http://www.plagiarism.org/ or https://www.copykiller.co.kr/notice to get more information on plagiarism and how to avoid it)  ⬥Multiple Submissions: Submitting the same work for credit more than once without the express permission of the professor.   ⬥Any student who knowingly helps another student violate these academic behavior standards is also in violation of the standards.
detail.LT_POLY: Professionalism Policy  Per university policy and classroom etiquette, mobile phones and similar devices must be silenced during all classroom sessions. Also, the use of Kakao Talk or similar instant messaging applications is limited to communication or sharing of documents with partners in class. Those not following these rules will be warned, may receive participation credit deductions, be marked as absent, or be asked to leave the classroom to avoid disrupting the learning environment. Students who habitually disturb the class may receive a warning, and ultimately could receive a failing grade.  The use of Machine Translation and AI Generation (Google translate, Papago, Chat GPT, etc.) is allowed for personal use to assist students with content understanding and developmental phases of the writing process. However, directly copying and pasting Machine Translator output is prohibited. Furthermore, copying and pasting Machine Translated or AI Generated content may also result in accidental plagiarism, poor/incorrect word choice, or other problems that may result in point deductions.

Students are expected to use only English for all class activities.

detail.LT_POLY:
Attendance Policy
All classes are mandatory and must be attended. If you are unable to attend class, you must inform your professor at least 24 hours prior to your intended absence. If you have a reasonable excuse for your absence you will be given an excused absence. An excused absence does not negatively affect your final grade, however repeated absences (excused or not) may result in a warning from your professor, after which any further absences may lead to being awarded a failing or incomplete grade in the course.
If you miss class due to ill-health, provide a medical certificate to your professor on the first class meeting after your return to receive your excused absence. If you are absent without a reasonable excuse, you will be marked absent from the class meeting. If you are marked absent 4 or more times during the semester you will receive a failing grade for the course.
Please arrive on time for all class meetings. Three late arrivals will result in being marked as an unexcused absence. Arriving more than 20 minutes after the start of class will automatically be marked as an unexcused absence.
 
Late Work Policy
There are no make-ups for work completed in class, such as group work or presentations. Any work not completed during class time must be finished and turned in by the due date set by your professor.
If you are absent (even if you have a reasonable excuse), it is your responsibility to find out what work was assigned during the classes you missed and to complete that work by the due date. Failure to submit work by the due date is unacceptable, and the work will not receive any feedback.
Group Work Policy
Everyone must take part in group projects. For daily work throughout the semester, you will be assigned to a group. All members of a group will receive the same score. In other words, the assignment is given 1 score, and everyone in the group receives it. For larger assignments and projects, you may work in groups but be assessed individually.
Student/Professor Communication
If you have a question regarding the course administration or course content you should:
⬥Ask your professor during or after class. Because it is common for many students to have the same questions, asking in class allows every student to get the answer at the same time.
⬥Ask your professor via email if you have a private question.
Your professor will designate time each week specifically for helping students.
⬥Your professor will post an appointment sheet on or near their office door. To make an appointment, sign up for the time you wish to visit.
⬥Alternatively, you can send an email to your professor to make an appointment. 
⬥Outside of office hours, your professor may be busy attending to other duties, so they may not be available to meet.

detail.LT_SUMA: The following outline looks somewhat ambitious and we probably will not be  able to cover all the topics listed below. If we slip behind the schedule, then  we will either skim over or just omit some of the topics.    I. The Bassics of Economics (Ch. 1,2,3,4, and 5)  1. Introduction to Economics  2. Exchange and Production  3, Demand and Supply    II. Markets and Government’s Interventions (Ch. 6, 7, and 8)  III. The Consumer Theory (Ch. 21)  1. The Basic of the Consumer Theory  2. A Consumer’s Optimal Choice  3. Demand Function  IV. The Production Theory (Ch. 13, and 14)  1. The Basics of the Production Theory  2. A Competitive Firm’s Profit Maximization
detail.LT_PURO: This course is designed to  teach the students the very basic stuffs of economics especially focusing on  microeconomics such as (1) how consumers and firms make their economic  decisions (i.e., demand and supply), (2) how the equilibrium prices are de￾termined in the competitive market. Although the level of this course is an  introductory level, the students should expect that some mathemat￾ical and statistical tools will be used in the class. However, economic  intuition will be more emphasized during the course because having such  economic intuition is much more important for understanding economics.  The students are encouraged to raise their questions and to express their  opinions on the subjects during the class time. However, the students are  not allowed to talk with others about irrelevant subjects during the  class time. In fact, all the discussions in the class will be conducted  by me. And, the students who offend this rule will be penalized  severely. The students are recommended to try the problem sets themselves  first. But, sharing your own idea with other students is another good way  of developing your knowledge on the topics. Students are also strongly en￾couraged to make use of my official office hours to discuss classwork. If you  cannot make the office hours, we can make special arrangements.
detail.LT_POLY: YOUR MOBILE PHONE SHOULD BE TURNED OFF DUR￾ING THE CLASS TIME.
detail.LSN_MTHD: THE STUDENTS SHOULD MAKE GROUPS. THE MAXI￾MUM NUMBER OF STUDENTS IN EACH GROUP IS 5. THE  PROBLEM SETS WILL BE AND SHOULD BE DONE ON A  GROUP BASIS.

detail.LT_SUMA: As science and technology play an increasingly significant role in shaping contemporary society, it is essential to develop a critical understanding of their nature and impacts. This course aims to cultivate students' ability to examine the characteristics and social implications of modern science and technology from multiple perspectives by introducing major theoretical discussions in Science and Technology Studies (STS), an interdisciplinary field that integrates diverse approaches from the humanities and social sciences. Building on these theoretical foundations, students will engage in discussions of contemporary issues and debates related to science and technology.
detail.LT_PURO:
The primary objective of this course is to enable students to develop a solid
understanding of the characteristics of modern science and technology and to critically examine their social implications. Throughout the course, students will engage in critical reflection on modern science and technology using diverse perspectives and theoretical frameworks from the humanities and social sciences. Students will also develop the ability to articulate and communicate their own informed views effectively on contemporary issues related to science and technology.
detail.LRN_ITGT: Failure to satisfy the minimum attendance requirement or any form of academic misconduct, including plagiarism, may result in a final grade of F, regardless of performance on examinations or course assignments.
detail.LT_POLY: The course is designed for both Korean and international students and is conducted primarily in English. While course materials and lectures are provided mainly in English, the use of English and Korean in lectures, discussions, and question-and-answer sessions may be adjusted according to the linguistic backgrounds and needs of the enrolled students.
detail.ALL_CNTN:
Week 1: Introduction to Science and Technology Studies: Key Questions in STS
Week 2: The Emergence of Sociology of Scientific Knowledge
Week 3: Laboratory Studies and Actor-Network Theory
Week 4: Contemporary Science in Practice: Screening and discussion of <Naturally Obsessed>
Week 5: The Social Shaping of Technology
Week 6: Screening and discussion of <Who Killed the Electric Car?>
Week 7: Risk Governance in the Era of Post-Normal ScienceWeek 
8: Midterm Examination
Week 9: Emerging Technology in Everyday Life: Screening and discussion of <In the Family>
Week 10: Science, Technology, and Gender
Week 11: Screening and discussion of <Hidden Figures>
Week 12: Academic, Social, and Ethical Dimensions of Scientists’ Work
Week 13: Screening and discussion of <The Hwang Scandal>
Week 14: Group Presentations: Book Review and Critical Analysis
Week 15: Final Examination

detail.LT_SUMA: This course aims to understand and discuss modern and contemporary world history from a comparative history perspective.
detail.LT_PURO: This course explores major themes and events in modern and contemporary world history through a comparative historical approach. By examining revolutions, imperialism, world wars, the Cold War, Students will develop a broader understanding of how historical processes have shaped the modern and contemporary world. Through group discussion, students will also develop critical thinking skills and deepen their understanding of history. on. In addition, the course encourages students to critically examine historical representations, memory, and competing interpretations of the past in various media.
detail.ETC: Lecture slides will serve as the primary course material, with supplementary materials provided as needed.

detail.LSN_MTHD: Each topic consists of a two-week module: one week of lecture followed by one week of review and discussion.

detail.LT_SUMA: 이 강좌에서는 대학에서의 학술 활동에 필요한 논리적·비판적 글쓰기와 사고 능력을 기른다. 학술 글쓰기를 위한 기초적인 정서법과 문단 구성에서부터 주제 구상과 설계 및 내용 조직, 집필에 이르는 글쓰기의 구체적인 방법을 단계별로 학습하고 직접 글로 쓰는 과정을 거친다. 이와 함께 다양한 텍스트를 섭렵하고, 발표, 토론 및 상호 논평(peer review) 활동을 종합적으로 수행한다.
detail.LT_PURO: - 학술 글쓰기의 기본적인 형식과 내용 요건, 수행 과정에 대한 지식을 습득하고, 학술적 에세이, 연구 계획서 등 다양한 종류의 글쓰기를 직접 경험한다.  - 창의적인 연구 주제를 수립하고, 세부 연구 계획을 논리적으로 설계하는 팀 프로젝트를 수행한다.  - 텍스트 깊이 읽기와 토론, 글쓰기, 상호 논평을 통해 동료와 함께 지식을 탐구하여 결론에 이르는 학술적 논의와 협업의 과정을 경험한다.   - 학술적 논의가 요구되는 현상과 사실, 개념과 원리, 법칙과 이론에 대해 창의적·비판적으로 사고하고 해석하며, 그 과정과 내용을 논리적 글쓰기로 표현할 수 있는 역량을 기른다.
detail.ETC: 서울대학교 대학글쓰기1 교재편찬위원회 편, 『대학 글쓰기1』, 서울대학교출판문화원, 2026.
detail.LRN_ITGT: - 모든 과제물 작성 시 인용법, 주석과 참고 문헌 형식을 정확히 지켜야 하며, 연구 및 글쓰기 윤리를 준수하도록 한다.  - 표절 또는 도용한 과제는 0점 처리한다.  - 모든 제출물에 대하여 AI 프로그램 활용 여부를 검사하며, AI 프로그램으로 작성한 경우 표절 및 도용으로 간주한다.
detail.LT_POLY: - 중간고사는 01, 02, 03, 04, 05분반 공통 논술형 지필 고사로 시행하며, 기말고사는 팀 프로젝트 결과물로 대체한다.  - 팀 프로젝트 수업 중 토론과 상호 논평(peer review)이 진행되며, 이를 수업 참여도 성적에 반영한다.  - office hour를 이용하여 수업 및 과제에 대한 개별 상담을 받을 수 있다.   - 과제물은 기한 내에 제출해야 하며, 기한을 넘긴 과제물은 감점을 받는다.  - 과제물 제출은 LMS 과제함 제출을 원칙으로 하며, 제출 여부를 반드시 확인하여 불이익이 없도록 한다.

detail.LRN_ITGT:
상호 존중의 원칙 하에 자유로운 의견 개진과 건설적인 토론이 진행될 수 있도록 노력할 것.
건전한 의견 개진이 아닌 타인에 대한 비난, 수업 방해 등의 행위 시 교수의 제제가 있을 수 있음. 
수업의 구성원에 대한 괴롭힘이나 폭력 등에 행위는 엄히 금지하며, 필요시 학칙에 따라 조치함. 
과제와 시험에서 부정이 발견될 시 학칙에 따라 조치함.
detail.LT_POLY:
학습 보조를 목적으로 하는 IT기기 사용 가능.

detail.LT_SUMA: <글로벌문화와 의사소통Introduction to Intercultural Communication>은 문화와 문화 간 의사소통에 대한 다양한 관점과 사례를 검토함으로써 1)자기 자신(의 문화)에 대한 이해를 돕고, 나아가 2)성공적인 문화간 소통에 필요한 언어적, 문화적 감수성과 실천 의지를 기르는 것을 목적으로 한다. 문화를 특정 민족/국가의 고유한 특성으로 간주하는 본질주의적 시각에 대한 비판적 검토와 더불어 문화의 역동적, 역사적, 정치적, 담론적인 성격에 주목한다. 이를 위해 전반부에 문화에 대한 차원적인 이해 관점에서 출발하여 Adrian Holliday의 문화간 의사소통 이론을 집중적으로 살핀다. 학기 후반부에는 ‘국제공용어로서의 영어(학습)’과 ‘해외연수’ 등 한국 대학생의 삶과 밀접한 관계가 있는 주제를 문화 간 의사소통의 관점에서 탐색한다. 마지막 4주 동안은 ‘디지스트 커뮤니티에 존재하는 문화적 갈등/충돌과 해결방안’을 주제로 ‘문제중심학습(PBL, Problem Based Learning)’을 활용, 학생들 스스로 문제를 정의하고 탐색하여 해결책을 제안하는 프로젝트를 진행함으로써, 문화간 의사소통의 이론과 실제에 대한 이해의 깊이를 더한다.
detail.LT_PURO: <수업내용>    - 문화에 대한 다양한 관점(비/본질주의적 관점)을 이해하고 차별점을 안다.    - 문화 간 의사소통의 다양하고 역동적인 차원을 이론적, 실천적 관점에서 이해한다.  - Adrian Holliday의 문화 간 소통 이론을 인지적, 실천적 차원에서 이해한다.  - 자문화와 문화적 정체성에 대해 비판적으로 성찰한다.  - 세계 공용어로서의 영어와 원어민/비원어민 담론을 문화적, 역사적, 정치적 맥락에서 이해한다.  - 대학생 해외연수의 목적, 수행, 어려움 등의 문제를 문화 간 의사 소통의 관점에서 이해한다.     - 궁극적으로 성공적인 문화간 의사소통을 위한 언어적, 문화적 감수성과 자신감을 기른다.   <수업문화>    - 어떤 의견이든 말할 수 있는 자유롭고 안전한 공간을 교수자와 학생이 함께 만들어 나간다.       - 다른 사람의 의견은 자신과 다를 수 있으며, 다르다고 틀린 것이 아니라는 점을 늘 상기한다.      - 다른 이의 의견을 경청하고, 건설적이고 진정함이 묻어나는 피드백을 제공한다.       - 하나일 때 보다 함께일 때 더욱 풍부한 사고를 실천할 수 있음을 깨닫는다.
detail.ETC: !! 중요: 보충자료 등은 가급적 우리말 자료를 사용하고자 하나, 주교재가 영어 원서임.

detail.LT_SUMA: 본 과목은 1학년 신입생들이 대학 생활에 성공적으로 적응하고 자신의 진로와 전공을 설계할 수 있도록 지원하는 데 목적을 둔다. 특히 진로탐색 및 전공설계 I에서는 학교생활 안내, 트랙별 교과 및 진로 설명, 멘토링 제도 등을 통해 학생들이 학교 자원과 네트워크를 효과적으로 활용하도록 돕고, 각 트랙의 학문적 특성을 이해함으로써 다양한 학문적 선택지를 탐색할 수 있도록 하며, 저명한 학자를 초청한 특별 세미나를 통해 학생들의 학문적 시야를 넓히게 한다.
detail.LT_PURO: 학생들의 대학생활 적응을 지원하고, 각 트랙의 학문 분야와 주요 연구 분야를 소개하여 학생들이 희망하는 학문 분야에 대한 이해를 높이고, 사회 및 학문분야 리더의 강의를 통해 세상을 바라보는 시야를 넓히는 것을 목적으로 한다.
detail.LRN_ITGT: 표절은 다른 사람의 아이디어 또는 정확한 문구를 출처 없이 복사하는 것으로, 이는 심각한 학문적 위반입니다. 따라서 학기말에 제출하는 전공 설계 보고서 작성 시 표절이 발생하지 않도록 주의해야 합니다.

detail.LT_SUMA: This course aims to introduce the causes, background, and historical development of South Korea’s foreign policy decisions. In particular, it focuses on discussing and analyzing South Korea’s security, trade, and unification policies, as well as its public diplomacy, in the post-Korean War era.
detail.LT_PURO: This course has two primary objectives: first, to provide an overview of Korea's unique context of division and unification; and second, to help students develop a understanding of contemporary Korea in international relations.

detail.LT_SUMA: 21세기는 과학기술의 시대이다. 이제는 과학기술이 없는 삶을 상상할 수 없으며, 과학기술의 특징과 그 사회적 함의를 이해하는 것은 시민으로서 갖추어야 할 필수 자질이라고 할 수 있다. 현재 우리의 삶에 영향을 미치는 다양한 과학기술의 기원, 의미, 역할, 한계 등을 이해하기 위해서는 먼저 그것이 발전해 온 역사를 살펴볼 필요가 있다. 본 수업에서는 고대, 중세, 과학 혁명기를 거쳐 근대과학과 현대과학에 이르기까지 과학사의 긴 여정을 개괄적으로 살펴봄으로써, 과학기술이 어떤 과정을 통해 인류 문명에서 핵심적인 지위를 차지하게 되었는지를 이해할 것이다.
detail.LT_PURO: 이 수업에서 수강생들은 과학기술이 사회와 분리되어 독자적으로 존재하고 발전하는 것이 아니라 인간의 문명과 상호작용하면서 만들어져 온 것이라는 점을 이해하게 될 것이다. 이를 통해, 수강생들은 현대 과학기술의 특징과 사회적 함의를 비판적으로 사고할 수 있는 안목을 갖출 수 있다.
detail.ETC: 본 수업의 목적은 과학기술의 발전 과정에 대한 이해에 기반하여 수강생들로 하여금 현대 과학기술의 특징과 사회적 함의를 비판적으로 성찰할 수 있게끔 만드는 것이며, 이를 효율적으로 달성하기 위한 과제들이 마련되어 있다. (1) 강의 내용에 대한 이해를 평가하기 위해 중간시험, 기말시험을 실시한다. 간단한 서술식 문항들에 대해 정해진 시간 안에 스스로 답안지를 작성하여 제출. (2) 수강생들은 학기 중 과학사 및 관련 인접 분야(과학학 전반)의 책을 조별로 1권 골라 함께 읽고 수업 시간에 발표한다. 책 선정 방식 및 서평 제출일자는 수업 시간에 설명할 예정. (3) 수강생들은 몇몇 주차에 수업 시간 내 이루어지는 조별 토론에 참여하며, 토론 결과를 간략히 정리하여 발표하여야 한다.  * 성적 평가 비율: 출석 10%, 중간시험 30%, 기말시험 30%, 조별 과제 30%
detail.LRN_ITGT: 출석일수 부족, 표절 등 부정행위시 시험 및 과제물 성적과 무관하게 F학점을 받을 수 있다.
detail.LSN_MTHD: 본 강의는 대구경북과학기술원(DGIST)에서 과학기술을 학습하고 그 세부적인 기술적 능력을 훈련하고 있는 대학 학부생들을 위해 개설되었다. 다양한 분야의 글을 읽고 이해하는 것에 큰 문제가 없는 학생이라면 어렵지 않게 강의 내용을 파악할 수 있다.     매주 수업은 전반부와 후반부로 나누어진다. 수업 전반부에서는 담당 교수가 해당 주에 다루는 주요 주제와 내용을 설명하는 강의를 진행한다. 수업 후반부에서는 수업에서 다룬 주요 주제에 대한 조별 토론과 간략한 발표를 진행하거나(6주 이상), 수강생의 서평에 대한 발표를 듣고 토의할 예정이다. 수강생들은 학기 초에 자신의 관심사에 맞춰 과학사 분야의 책을 한 권 골라 읽고, 다른 수강생들에게 해당 책의 내용을 설명하고 질의응답 시간을 갖는다. 이러한 수업 방식을 통해 과학사의 주요 주제들과 쟁점들을 체계적으로 다루면서도 수강생들이 자발적으로 과학사의 여러 주제들을 탐색하고 습득하도록 돕는다.

detail.LT_SUMA: 과학과 과학적 방법이 무엇인지 이해하고, 과학의 가치를 숙고하며, 과학과 사회가 어떻게 상호 영향을 주는지 살펴본다. 이러한 질문에 대해 과학철학자들이 제시한 답변을 살펴보고, 학생 스스로가 생각하는 답변을 논의할 것이다. 이를 통해서 ‘내가 경험한’ 과학을 되돌아 보고, 향후 과학자로서의 정체성과 윤리에 대해서 생각할 기회를 가지게 될 것이다.

detail.LT_PURO: 이 강의는 근대 사회의 형성과 전개 과정을 역사적 관점에서 살펴본다. 계몽주의, 혁명, 산업화, 제국주의, 세계대전, 냉전, 탈식민화 등 근현대 세계사의 주요 사건과 사상을 검토하며 현대 사회가 형성된 역사적 배경을 이해한다. 또한 역사적 사건과 사상이 사회에 미친 영향을 분석하고, 역사 재현과 기억의 문제를 비판적으로 검토함으로써 역사적 사고력과 성찰 능력을 함양하고자 한다.

detail.LT_SUMA: 이 강좌에서는 동서양의 지성사에 큰 영향을 미친 고전 텍스트를 읽고 토론한다. 특히 이번 학기에 다루는 작품들은 유토피아와 디스토피아를 주요 주제로 삼고 있으며, 각 시대의 사상가와 작가들이 인간과 사회, 권력과 질서에 대해 어떠한 문제를 제기하고 어떤 대안을 상상했는지를 살펴본다. 인공지능, 생명공학, 데이터 기술 등 과학기술의 발전이 인간과 사회를 빠르게 변화시키고 있는 오늘날, 우리는 기술이 만들어 갈 미래에 대해 더욱 풍부한 상상력과 비판적 성찰을 요구받고 있다. 이러한 문제의식에 따라 본 강좌에서는 16세기부터 21세기에 이르는 고전 텍스트를 함께 읽으며, 인간, 사회, 권력, 과학기술의 관계를 탐구하고 더 나은 미래에 대한 다양한 비전과 그 한계를 탐색한다. 수업은 학생 중심의 읽기와 토론을 기반으로 진행된다. 학생들은 매주 지정된 분량의 텍스트를 읽고 질문을 작성하며, 수업 시간에는 이를 바탕으로 조별 및 전체 토론을 진행한다. 이를 통해 고전 텍스트를 역사적 산물로 이해하는 데 그치지 않고, 오늘날의 과학기술과 사회가 직면한 문제들을 비판적으로 검토하고자 한다.
detail.LT_PURO:
- 유토피아 및 디스토피아를 다루는 주요 고전 텍스트를 읽고 그 역사적 맥락과 핵심 쟁점을 이해한다.
- 고전 텍스트에 나타난 인간, 사회, 권력, 과학기술에 대한 관점을 비판적으로 분석한다.
- 서로 다른 시대와 장르의 텍스트를 비교하며 유토피아와 디스토피아에 대한 다양한 상상력을 탐구한다.
- 토론과 글쓰기를 통해 자신의 관점을 정교화하고 다양한 해석과 관점을 비판적으로 검토한다.
- 고전 텍스트를 바탕으로 과학기술이 인간과 사회에 미치는 영향을 성찰하고 미래 사회의 가능성과 한계를 탐구한다.
detail.LRN_ITGT: 표절: 독서보고서를 작성할 때 주어진 텍스트를 참조할 경우 반드시 그 쪽수를 괄호 안에 기입한다. 그 외에 다른 사람의 견해를 참조하려 한다면(책, 논문, 정기간행물 기사, 인터넷 자료) 반드시 출처를 쪽수까지 정확하게 각주에 기록한다. 인터넷 자료는 참고한 대목을 확인할 수 있도록 해당 주소와 참조 일자를 각주에 기록한다. 다른 사람이 쓴 글을 그대로 빌려올 경우 반드시 큰 따옴표 또는 별도 문단으로 인용하고, 각주에 출처를 기록한다. 큰 따옴표나 별도 문단으로 인용하지 않고 다른 사람이 쓴 어구나 문장을 그대로 쓸 경우 각주에 출처를 표시하더라도 표절로 간주한다. 이 같은 간접인용의 경우는 반드시 필자 본인의 문장으로 바꿔 쓰고, 출처를 각주에 기록해야 한다. 표절이 확인되면 무조건 F학점을 부여한다.
detail.LT_POLY: 출석: 수강생은 강의 일정에 따라 반드시 수업에 참석해야 한다. 결석이 불가피한 사유(예: 가족의 사망과 중병, 수강생 본인의 입원, 천재지변)가 없다면 모두 결석으로 간주한다. 사소한 질병으로 인한 결석을 포함해서 결석이 2회를 초과하면 F학점을 부여한다. 일반적인 질병으로 인한 외래 진료 확인서를 받지 않는다.
detail.LSN_MTHD: 본 교과목은 학생 중심의 세미나 및 토론 방식으로 운영된다. 학생들은 매주 지정된 읽기 자료를 바탕으로 질문을 작성하여 제출하고, 수업 시간에는 학생들이 제기한 질문을 중심으로 조별 및 전체 토론을 진행한다. 교수자는 토론을 촉진하고 주요 쟁점을 정리하는 역할을 수행하며, 학생들은 다양한 해석과 관점을 검토하면서 텍스트를 심층적으로 탐구한다.

detail.LT_SUMA:
The theme of this course for Fall 2026 is Science, Technology, and Society. The course has two main objectives: (1) to improve students’ English language skills and (2) to explore the socio-political implications of science and technology through reading and discussing science fiction in English.
From a language-learning perspective, the course is grounded in the view of language as a social practice. Rather than studying English in isolation, students will engage with literary texts that present authentic social situations, conflicts, and perspectives. Through reading, discussion, and writing, students will develop their ability to understand and use English in meaningful contexts.
In terms of content, science fiction provides a valuable lens through which to examine the relationship between science, technology, and society. By imagining technologically advanced futures, science fiction invites readers to reflect on the social, political, and economic consequences of scientific and technological change. Throughout the semester, students will critically examine these issues while considering their own future roles as scientists and engineers.
Students will read three to four science fiction texts: one short story and two to three novelettes or novels. The texts will be selected by students from a shortlist during the first week of the semester.
detail.LT_PURO:
<Language Aspects>
Cultivate authentic long-text reading by reading literary texts in English for pleasure and meaning. 
Enhance vocabulary power and sentential and discoursal understanding through increased exposure to vocabulary and sentence structures used in real life. 
Develop English presentation skills by preparing a presentation in English on a given part of a text.  
Develop academic English writing skills by writing a source-based essay in English on a self-selected topic related to 'Science & Technology and Society'.
<Content aspect>
Understand the relationship between science fiction and science and technology. 
Identify the technological advances needed to make the futures projected in science fiction possible and examine the current state of those technologies. 
Critically examine the role of science and technology in social, political, and economic aspects. 
Reflect on one's own role as a future scientist/engineer with a focus on the socio-political dimension of science and technology.
<Class Culture of Learning>
The instructor and the students together create a free and safe space where everyone can voice an opinion. 
It is natural that others' opinions may differ from your own, and being different doesn't mean wrong. 
We listen to others carefully and exchange constructive and genuine feedback with each other
detail.LRN_ITGT:
Academic dishonesty of any kind is strictly prohibited and will result in a grade of U/F if caught. Academic dishonesty includes the following:   
Attendance-related cheating (such as proxy attendance)  
Cheating on assignments and presentations (failure to credit sources, plagiarism, submitting the same assignment to more than one class without prior permission)  
Aiding or abetting a classmate in cheating
Use of Generative AI 
Generative AI tools (e.g., ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini) may be used for brainstorming, language support, and revision. However, all submitted work must represent the student's own thinking and analysis. Students are responsible for verifying the accuracy of AI-generated content and must acknowledge substantial AI use in their assignments.
Students must include an AI Use Statement in all major assignments, including group presentations and the final essay. The AI Use Statement itself is not graded. However, failure to disclose substantial AI use or intentionally misrepresenting AI use may be considered academic dishonesty.
detail.LT_POLY:

2. Students will be reading 3-4 science fiction texts during  the semester.
ONE short story will be selected by students among the following two options:

Two or three longers texts will be selected from the following list:

detail.LSN_MTHD: With the exception of an introduction to the science fiction genre and literary criticism at the beginning of the semester, the instructor won't lecture and the class will be centered around reading and discussing the text in question. In this course, the instructor is not a "knowledge deliverer" but rather a "facilitator who helps in-class discussions and the emergence of collective intelligence". More specifically, the students will read the weekly assigned text before class and write a brief reflection on that section to share with others in class. The class will be organized around group presentations and discussions of relevant parts (including mini-presentations, discussion/debate, speaking/writing in role, and peer teaching). The class medium language is English.

detail.LT_SUMA: 현재 대한민국을 비롯한 세계 각국에서는 민주주의의 위기를 경험하고 있다. 대표적인 예로 극우세력의 준동과 포퓰리즘의 저변 확대는 정치적 양극화로 인한 대의 민주주의의 퇴행에서 비롯된 현상이다. 정당은 대의 민주주의의 핵심제도로서 민주주의의 위기는 곧 정당의 위기로 치환될 수 있다. 따라서 한국 민주주의의 실제를 정당정치의 관점에서 체계적으로 분석하고 비판적으로 성찰하는 일은 지속가능한 민주주의를 모색하는데 있어서 필수적인 것이다. 따라서 대한민국 제1공화국 시기부터 현재까지의 정치사와 정당구도에 대한 이해가 필수적이며, 정당의 분류와 기능, 정당조직, 선거제도와 정당체제, 이념, 후보선택, 선거 캠페인, 정책형성, 정부와의 관계와 같은 정당에 대한 이론적 관점들을 명확하게 이해하는 것이 필요하다. 이 과정에서 한국 민주주의의 역사와 정당정치의 여러 문제들을 인식함으로써 학생들이 궁극적으로 정당정치의 본질에 대해서 생각해볼 수 있는 기회를 가질 수 있기를 기대한다.
detail.LT_PURO: 본 교과목은 대한민국 정부의 수립 이후 한국 정당정치의 역사와 정당체제, 정당조직, 정책형성, 선거 캠페인, 후보자 선택, 정부와의 관계와 같은 이론적 분석을 결합하여 한 사람의 시민으로서 한국의 민주주의의 실제를 통찰할 수 있는 역량을 기르는 것을 목표로 한다.

detail.LT_SUMA: This course aims to help students understand the characteristics of global regions and develop the ability to analyze them from a geographical perspective. In an era of globalization that demands creative thinking, the course examines the diverse economic, social, and cultural interactions that shape regions around the world, as well as the natural environments in which they exist. Drawing on foundational concepts from the social sciences, the course fosters a broad understanding of cultural and spatial diversity through the study of world geography.
detail.LT_PURO: To enhance students’ understanding of the world by comparing cultural patterns, population dynamics, and political and economic systems across different regions of the globe.  To foster geographic thinking and analytical skills through the critical examination of key theories and methods in the social sciences, with particular attention to human–environment interactions, spatial processes, and connections among world regions.  To develop students’ ability to examine geographic issues critically and to cultivate a balanced understanding of the interrelationships, diversity, and distinctiveness of global cultures.
detail.LRN_ITGT: Academic misconduct, including plagiarism and cheating on examinations, may result in a failing grade (F) for this course. Unauthorized use of artificial intelligence (AI) tools in the preparation or completion of assessed work is prohibited and will result in an automatic failing grade (F) for the course.
detail.LT_POLY: Mobile phone use is not permitted during class. Students are expected to devote their full attention to course activities and lectures. Studying for other courses, completing assignments unrelated to this class, or engaging with non-course materials during class is not permitted. Students found doing so may be asked to leave the classroom immediately.    Regular attendance is required. Students who accumulate more than four absences may receive a failing grade (F) for the course.

detail.LT_SUMA: This course introduces students to the patterns and processes that shape the world's cultural systems, cultural landscapes, and built environments. Through the examination of scholarly research and theoretical perspectives in cultural geography, students will explore the cultural dimensions of landscape, place, and environment. The course addresses questions such as: How have cultural diffusion, race, and ethnicity influenced the ways we understand society and the world? How can we compare material and non-material culture, as well as folk and popular culture? Finally, how do language, religion, and cultural landscapes contribute to the formation of individual and collective identities? Through the study of cultural elements, values, and place-based experiences, students will develop an understanding of how identities are constructed and expressed across different cultural contexts.
detail.LT_PURO: Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to:    Analyze cultural texts and expressions of popular culture using key concepts and theoretical frameworks in cultural geography.  Critically evaluate major themes, debates, and subfields within cultural geography.  Apply concepts and perspectives from sociocultural geography to explore and interpret contemporary cultural phenomena.

detail.LT_SUMA: "Reading Poetry" provides a basic approach to the appreciation and analysis of poetry from thematic, theoretical, and historical perspectives. Throughout the course, students will read, write about, and discuss selected poems and essays on poetics from ancient Greek to contemporary times. Each class will consist of an oral presentation, group discussion, and lecture. As the title suggests, students may recite several lines from poems. By the end of the semester, students can expect to have developed a deeper understanding of poetry, and to have it become a part of their lives.
detail.LT_PURO: This course has three major aims: firstly, to enhance your understanding of poetry; secondly, to help you discover the joy of reading poetry; and finally, to encourage you to become a poet who can express and write about your everyday experiences

detail.LT_SUMA: The Scientific Writing course is designed to help students understand the fundamentals of effective scientific and technical writing and write a mini research paper as the final project. To this end, the course consists of two phases: Lecture/Discussion and the Writing Project. In the first quarter of the semester, students will learn the basics of academic research paper writing such as ethics and plagiarism, paraphrasing, referencing, and style; they will also explore the structure of scientific writing and discursive features specific to scientific writing by surveying published research papers in the science and technology fields. Equipped with this basic understanding about writing a research paper, students will move on to learn how to compose each of the sections of a research paper centering on content, frequently used vocabulary, discourse-organizing words, and syntax patterns. As they learn the specifics of each section, students will have ample opportunities to practice writing through not only structured class activities but also actually drafting their own research paper section by section according to the class progress.
detail.LT_PURO: The aim of this class is to help improve your scientific and technical writing skills. You should eventually be able to research, organize, and write technical and scientific material in a way that can be understood by your intended audiences.     By the end of this course: Students will be able to   - understand structure of scientific writing and its discursive features;   - write effectively, concisely, and clearly for an academic paper;   - write a short research paper of their interest; and   - demonstrate their understanding about ethics in the academic world.

detail.LT_SUMA:
This course is designed to help students understand the fundamentals of effective scientific and technical writing and to produce a short research paper as the final project. The course consists of two main phases: Lecture/Discussion and the Writing Project. In the first part of the semester, students learn the foundations of academic research writing such as research ethics and plagiarism, paraphrasing and referencing, academic style; they will also explore the structure of scientific writing and discursive features specific to scientific writing by surveying published research papers in the science and technology fields. Building on this foundation, students learn how to compose each section of a research paper centering on content development, key vocabulary, discourse organization, and relevant syntax. They draft their own papers step by step and engage in multiple rounds of revision through peer and instructor feedback. A process-oriented approach to writing is emphasized throughout the course.
The course also incorporates reflective engagement with digital writing tools. Students may use tools such as machine translation, generative AI, and other writing platforms to support their writing. At the end of the semester, students deliver a brief reflection on their writing process and digital tool use to promote transparency, responsibility, and awareness in academic writing.
detail.LT_PURO:
The aim of this class is to help improve your scientific and technical writing skills. You should eventually be able to research, organize, and write technical and scientific material in a way that can be understood by your intended audiences. 

By the end of this course: Students will be able to 
understand structure of scientific writing and its discursive features; 
write effectively, concisely, and clearly for an academic paper; 
write a short research paper of their interest; and 
demonstrate their understanding about ethics in the academic world.
critically and transparently monitor and reflect on their use of digital writing tools, including generative AI, while maintaining academic integrity and authorship.

detail.LT_SUMA:
- 현대 사회에 이르러 생명공학기술이 급속히 발전함에 따라 인류에게 다양한 혜택을 제공함과 동시에 인간 증강, GMO, 종의 다양성, 줄기세포와 복제, 팬더믹, 의료 빅데이터 등과 관련된 다양한 문제점 역시 발생시키고 있음. 
- 한편 생명과 관련된 사회적 이슈는 주제의 복잡성이 아주 커서 제대로 이해하고 대응하기 위해선 제반 생물학에 대한 이해뿐 아니라 다양한 학제를 아우르는 폭넓은 시야를 가질 필요가 있음. 
- 따라서 본 교과는 생명과 관련된 사회적 이슈를 이해하고 다루기 위해 각 이슈별로 관련 있는 제반 생명과학적 논의와 더불어 과학학, 과학사회학, 과학/기술철학, 생명윤리학, 과학기술정책론 등에 등장하는 논의 역시 다루고자 함.
detail.LT_PURO:
- 폭넓은 시야로 생명과학이 사회에 미치는 영향을 다면적으로 다룸으로써 생명과학 분야의 진로를 꿈꾸는 학생들에게 연구와 학업의 모티브를 제공하고, 연구를 통한 사회적 기여가 갖는 복합적 의미를 이해함으로써 미래 연구의 구체적 방향성을 설정하여 바람직한 비전을 설계할 수 있는 계기를 부여하고자 함.
- 비생명과학 분야 진로를 꿈꾸는 학생들의 경우에도 생명과 관련된 제반 이슈들은 생활 전반과 깊은 관련성이 있는 사안이므로 이러한 이슈에 대한 합리적 이해를 진작시키고, 이에 바탕하여 미래 시민사회의 구성원으로서 해당 이슈에 대한 적절한 대응을 하는데 필요한 지침들을 제공하고자 함. 
- 또한 먼 미래가 아니라 현안으로 발생하는 여러 생명 관련 쟁점에 대해 학부 생활을 하면서 어떤 관점을 견지하고, 그 이슈들에 어떠한 대응을 할지 구체적으로 가늠하여 실행해보는 장을 제공하고자 함. 
- 이를 통해 생명관련 제반 이슈에 대한 융합적 정보 습득 뿐 아니라 현 사회의 문제를 정의하고, 해결책을 모색하는 능력을 배양하며, 협업과 소통을 통해 문제 해결 방안을 수립하는 능력을 배양하고자 함.

detail.LT_SUMA: 분자생물학은 20세기 이후의 현대 생명과학을 형성하는 주요 패러다임을 정립하였다. 그리고, 분자생물학은 '실험과 사유'를 통해 발전한 학문 체계이다. 필연적으로, 분자생물학은 '실험'과 '이론'이 반드시 병행하는 교과목이다.   본 수업은 3학년 전공 필수 교과목으로 운영되는 분자생물학 이론 수업에 발 맞추어, 실험 교과목은 분자생물학 교과서에서도 자세하게 다루는 이론을 실제 프로젝트 수행 과정에서 구현하도록 학습한다. 다만, 모든 실험을 백화점 식으로 나열하는 학습법을 지양하고, 대부분의 생명과학 연구실 및 생명과학 기업에서 활발하게 사용하는 주요 분자생물학 기법을 학습하고자 한다.  즉, 분자생물학 실험 기법을 역사적으로 개괄하되, 현대 생명과학에서도 활발하게 활용되는 실험 기법(예, 클로닝 등)을 실습하고, 단순 체험을 넘어 기법의 주요 과정을 체득할 수 있도록 수업을 구성하였다.
detail.LT_PURO: 현대 분자생물학에 큰 영향을 미치고 있는 실험 기법을 파악하고, 실제 실험실에서 사용되고 있는 기법을 학생들이 직접 수행하면서 훈련한다.  - 연구 현장 및 기업에서 수요가 높은 실험 기법(클로닝, 생체분자 분리 정제, 기능 검증 시험 기법 등)을 실습  - 역사적으로 중요한 실험 기법(제한효소)의 발전과정 학습 및 실습  - 21세기에 개발된 최신 실험 기법(상동성 재조합)과 과거 실험 기법의 비교
