detail.LT_SUMA: 인체에 존재하는 내재면역과 적응면역이 발생하는 과정을 다양한 면역세포와 면역조절물질 간의 상호작용을 통해 이해한다.
detail.LT_PURO:
-내재면역과 적응면역에 대한 종합적 이해를 바탕으로 인체의 생리적, 병리적 현상을 면역학적으로 설명할 수 있다. 
-인체 현상에 대한 면역학적 이해를 바탕으로 여러 질병에 대처할 수 있는 방안에 대해 성찰할 수 있다.
detail.LRN_ITGT:
-출석은 학습활동의 성실성을 확인시켜 주는 가장 기본적인 행위이다. 따라서 출석확인 과정에서학생들의 정직성에 위배되는 대리출석, 무단조퇴 등을 하지 않는다. 
-과제물 작성 및 제출 과정에서 위변조, 표절, 중복제출을 금한다. 위조는 과제물의 내용을 거짓으로 만들어내는 행위를 말하며, 변조는 과제물의 내용을 자신에게 유리하게 바꾸는 행위를 말한다. 표절은 다른 사람의 아이디어, 연구 방법, 내용, 표현, 결과 등을 정확한 인용 없이 사용하는 행위를 뜻한다. 중복제출은 다른 교과목에서 이미 제출한 과제물을 새로 작성한 것처럼 제출하는 행위이다.
-시험에서의 부정행위를 금한다. 시험에서의 부정 행위란 시험에서 남의 답안을 보거나 허락되지 않은 참고자료를 보는 행위, 다른 사람에게 시험을 부탁하거나 다른 사람을 대신하여 시험을 보는 행위를 말한다.

detail.LT_SUMA: Mechanical engineers require a solid foundation in thermodynamics and the ability to analyze thermal systems for engineering design and problem-solving. This course introduces the fundamental principles of engineering thermodynamics and their applications to energy conversion systems. Topics include thermodynamic properties, energy and mass balances, the first and second laws of thermodynamics, entropy, control volume analysis, gas power cycles, vapor power cycles, refrigeration systems, and heat pump systems. A simple thermal engineering project will be conducted to reinforce theoretical concepts through practical engineering applications
detail.LT_PURO: Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to: 1) Understand and apply the fundamental principles of engineering thermodynamics. 2) Analyze closed and open systems using the first and second laws of thermodynamics. 3) Evaluate thermodynamic properties and entropy changes in engineering processes. 4) Analyze and compare gas power cycles, vapor power cycles, refrigeration systems, and heat pump systems. 5) Develop physical intuition and problem-solving skills through practical engineering examples and applications.

detail.LT_SUMA: This course provides an introduction to biomedical engineering for undergraduate students through team teaching by four instructors. Topics span wearable and soft robotics for human augmentation and rehabilitation, soft robotic implants and soft bioelectronics for minimally invasive neural interfaces, biomedical microrobots and robotic catheters, and brain-machine interfaces. Throughout the semester, the fundamental engineering principles underlying these biomedical applications will be covered.
detail.LT_PURO: Understanding the basic concepts of biomedical engineering in a variety of applications

detail.LT_SUMA: Artificial Intelligence is one of the most rapidly evolving subjects within the computing & engineering fields, with a special emphasis on creating intelligent robotic systems or applications. This course explains fundamental concepts of artificial intelligence to students who have no previous knowledge or experience with it.
detail.LT_PURO: The main goal of this course is to show students how to build intelligent systems drawing on techniques from information-based learning, Bayesian reasoning, nearest neighbor algorithm, regression, neural networks, convolutional neural networks, recurrent neural networks, and evolutionary computation. The principles behind these techniques are explained without resorting to complex mathematics, showing how the various techniques can be implemented for intelligent systems design.

detail.LT_SUMA: This course covers simultaneous understanding of the mechanical and electrical component characteristics. We will also learn design and analysis techniques of mechanical and electronic control systems, and construct and analyze real mechatronics systems using them. The contents of this course are as follows: (a) dynamic modeling and analysis on behavior of mechanical and electrical elements (b) motion control and analysis of the mechanical and electrical systems (c) robot mechatronics (d) measurement of physical quantities (acceleration, force, angle, torque etc.) and sensors via signal processing (e) artificial intelligence including machine/computer vision.

detail.LT_SUMA:
본 교과목은 생체모사(Bio-inspired) 비행 원리를 기반으로 하는 Flapping Bird Robot의 설계, 제작 및 제어를 수행하는 프로젝트 중심 교과목이다. 학생들은 조류의 비행 메커니즘과 기본적인 공기역학 및 기구학을 이해하고, CAD 설계, 3D 프린팅, 임베디드 시스템 및 센서 제어 기술을 활용하여 실제 플래핑 로봇을 개발한다. 또한 반복적인 설계 개선과 비행 실험을 통해 창의적 문제 해결 능력과 팀 기반 공학 설계 역량을 함양하며, 최종적으로 실제 비행 성능을 검증하고 평가하는 것을 목표로 한다.
This course is a project-based engineering design course focused on the design, fabrication, and control of bio-inspired flapping bird robots. Students will learn the fundamental principles of avian flight, including flight mechanics, basic aerodynamics, and kinematics, and apply CAD design, 3D printing, embedded systems, and sensor technologies to develop a functional flapping robot. Through iterative design improvements and experimental flight testing, students will cultivate creative problem-solving skills and team-based engineering design capabilities while validating and evaluating the flight performance of their robotic systems.
detail.LT_PURO:
본 교과목은 조류의 비행 원리와 플래핑 메커니즘에 대한 공학적 이해를 바탕으로 생체모사 비행로봇을 설계·제작·제어할 수 있는 능력을 배양하는 것을 목표로 한다. 학생들은 기계설계, 구조 설계, 임베디드 시스템, 센서 및 액추에이터 제어, 실험 및 성능 분석 과정을 통합적으로 수행하며, 팀 프로젝트를 통해 창의적 설계 능력과 협업 역량을 함양하고 실제 공학 문제를 해결하는 경험을 습득한다.
The objective of this course is to develop students' ability to design, fabricate, and control bio-inspired flapping bird robots based on an engineering understanding of avian flight principles and flapping mechanisms. Students will integrate mechanical and structural design, embedded systems, sensor and actuator control, experimental testing, and performance analysis throughout the project. Through team-based engineering design projects, they will enhance their creativity, collaboration skills, and practical problem-solving abilities while gaining hands-on experience in addressing real-world engineering challenges.

detail.LT_SUMA:
This is an application-oriented course on solving materials science and engineering problems with data and machine learning (ML). The first half provides a compact treatment of materials data preprocessing and statistics; regression, classification, and unsupervised learning; model validation and uncertainty; and deep learning (MLP, CNN, GNN, generative models). The second half goes deeper into real research applications: property-prediction pipelines, interpretable ML and design-rule discovery, inverse design via Bayesian optimization, machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIP), image-based microstructure analysis, and literature mining with language models.
이 교과는 재료과학·공학 문제를 데이터와 기계학습(ML)으로 다루는 방법을 배우는 응용 중심 과목이다. 전반부에서는 재료 데이터의 전처리·통계, 회귀·분류·비지도 학습, 모델 검증과 불확실성, 딥러닝(MLP·CNN·GNN·생성모델)의 핵심 원리를 압축적으로 다룬다. 후반부에서는 물성예측 파이프라인, 해석가능 ML과 설계규칙 발견, Bayesian optimization 기반 역설계, 머신러닝 원자간 퍼텐셜(MLIP), 이미지 기반 미세구조 분석, 문헌 마이닝·언어모델 등 재료 연구의 실제 응용 문제를 다룬다.
detail.LT_PURO:
Formulate materials datasets into problem-appropriate representations such as data matrices, descriptors, images, graphs, and text.  Connect the core principles of regression, classification, dimensionality reduction, deep learning, GNNs, Bayesian optimization, and interpretable ML to materials problems and design suitable approaches.  Identify and diagnose reliability pitfalls in applied ML, including data leakage, extrapolation, faulty validation splits, uncertainty, and misinterpretation.  Critically read representative application studies (property prediction, inverse design, simulation acceleration, image/literature analysis) and assess the validity and limitations of the methods.  Independently construct and describe an ML approach — covering data, representation, model, and validation — for a given materials problem.  
재료 데이터셋을 데이터 행렬, 디스크립터, 이미지, 그래프, 텍스트 등 문제에 맞는 표현으로 정식화한다.
회귀, 분류, 차원축소, 딥러닝, GNN, Bayesian optimization, 해석가능 ML의 핵심 원리를 재료 문제에 연결하여 적용 방안을 설계한다.
데이터 누수, 외삽, 검증 분할 오류, 불확실성, 해석 오류 등 ML 적용 시의 신뢰성 함정을 식별하고 진단한다.
물성예측·역설계·시뮬레이션 가속·이미지/문헌 분석 등 대표 응용 사례를 비판적으로 읽고, 방법의 타당성과 한계를 평가한다.
주어진 재료 문제에 대해 데이터·표현·모델·검증을 포함한 ML 접근 전략을 스스로 구성하고 서술한다.

detail.LT_SUMA: This introductory course provides fundamental knowledge for understanding ceramic materials, with emphasis on advanced ceramics. Beginning with the definition and classification of ceramics, the course examines atomic bonding, crystal structures, defect chemistry, diffusion, and phase stability. Students will learn how these physicochemical phenomena govern the dielectric, magnetic, optical, and related functional properties of ceramics, and how structure–property relationships can be interpreted from a materials science perspective. In addition, the course includes computer-assisted visualization of materials structures, computer-based thermodynamic analysis and phase-diagram plotting, and visualization and analysis of ceramic-property data.
detail.LT_PURO: After completing this course, students will be able to: (1) explain the definition, classification, and major categories of ceramics; (2) understand fundamental physicochemical phenomena in ceramics, including defects, nonstoichiometry, and atomic transport; (3) relate crystal structure, defect chemistry, diffusion, and phase stability to ceramic properties; (4) explain dielectric, magnetic, and optical properties from the viewpoint of ceramic structure and bonding; (5) use computer tools to visualize ceramic structures and interpret thermodynamic trends, phase diagrams, and property data; and (6) analyze advanced ceramics using a structure–property framework grounded in the fundamentals of ceramic materials science.

detail.LT_SUMA: Thermal and statistical physics deals with systems composed of approximately 1023 particles, such as air, water, electrons in metals, and photons from the sun. This course explores macroscopic physical quantities—including temperature, pressure, volume, heat capacity, magnetism, and engine efficiency—and explains them using microscopic principles and probabilistic concepts of statistical physics. We begin with the basic concepts of thermodynamics, such as heat, temperature, and the laws of thermodynamics, and apply them to heat engines and phase transitions. The course also introduces classical and quantum statistics as tools for a deeper understanding of various physical phenomena.

detail.LT_SUMA: With Classical Mechanics as a prerequisite, this course aims to provide a deeper understanding of various topics in classical mechanics and to develop analytical methods for solving related problems. Mathematical tools such as differential equations, multivariable calculus, linear algebra, and related subjects will be introduced and utilized throughout the course. Prior knowledge of these analytical methods is not required, but is recommended before or during the course. The motion of rigid bodies will be covered in depth based on Newtonian mechanics. Lagrangian and Hamiltonian mechanics will also be introduced to provide a foundation for understanding modern physics, including quantum mechanics.
detail.LT_PURO: Understand Newtonian mechanics and apply its concepts to solve problems using analytical methods. Understand the formalisms of Lagrangian and Hamiltonian mechanics.

detail.LT_SUMA: This course will introduce Einstein’s theory of gravitation from a mathematical point of view. Basic concepts of differential geometry will be developed alongside basic concepts of general relativity. The main focus of the course will be on the definition of mathematical concepts, the study of their properties and relations, and their illustration in terms of physical examples.
detail.LT_PURO: After completing this course, the students should have a clear understanding of fundamental concepts of differential geometry (manifolds, metrics, connections, geodesics and the curvature tensor) and general relativity (spacetime and causality, the equivalence principle and the Einstein field equations), their relation, and their application in the description of basic models in cosmology.

detail.LT_SUMA:
본 과목의 목표는 양자전산의 개념과 중요한 양자 알고리듬을 이해하고, 양자 컴퓨터나 에뮬레이터를 이용해서 간단한 양자 알고리듬을 구현해보는 것이다.
(The objective of this course is to understand the concepts of quantum computing and important quantum algorithms, and to implement simple quantum algorithms using a quantum computer or an emulator.)
detail.LT_PURO:
이 강의가 목표하고자 하는 바는 다음과 같다:

1. 양자 전산의 기반이 되는 양자 역학의 핵심 개념(상태 벡터, 중첩, 얽힘, 유니터리 연산 등)을 이해한다.
2. 양자 논리 게이트의 특성을 수학적으로 서술하고, 이를 바탕으로 기초적인 양자 회로를 설계 및 분석한다.
3. 주요 양자 알고리즘의 동작 과정을 이해하고, 고전 전산 대비 양자 시스템이 가지는 성능적 이점을 비교 분석한다.
4. 실제 양자 하드웨어 플랫폼의 물리적 구현 원리와 시스템의 특성을 파악한다.
5. 양자 에뮬레이터 및 클라우드 기반 양자 컴퓨터를 활용하여 양자 알고리즘을 직접 프로그래밍하고 구동 결과를 검증한다.

(By the end of this course, students will be able to:

1. Understand the core concepts of quantum mechanics underlying quantum computing (state vectors, superposition, entanglement, unitary operations, etc.).
2. Mathematically describe the characteristics of quantum logic gates, and design and analyze basic quantum circuits based on this.
3. Understand the operation processes of major quantum algorithms, and comparatively analyze the performance advantages of quantum systems over classical computing.
4. Grasp the physical implementation principles and system characteristics of actual quantum hardware platforms.
5. Directly program quantum algorithms and verify the execution results using quantum emulators and cloud-based quantum computers.)

detail.LT_SUMA: This course surveys modern perspectives on the fundamental constituents of matter and their interactions. Utilizing Quantum Field Theory (QFT) as a foundational framework, the course emphasizes practical results and conceptual understanding. While this is not a full QFT course, we will use its results to understand particle physics, meaning familiarity with classical mechanics and quantum mechanics is sufficient. Students will analyze the structure and content of the Standard Model, explore its cross-disciplinary connections to other fields of physics, and examine the theoretical motivations for pushing beyond its boundaries.
detail.LT_PURO: The first part of the semester we will focus on the formal structure of the Standard Model. We will build up necessary mathematical tools for treatment of symmetries, special relativity, relativistic Lagrangians and equations of motion for scalar, spinor and vector fields, the principle of local gauge invariance and the Higgs mechanism for mass generation. Equipped with these tools,. in the second part of the course will focus more on computational aspects of QFT. Such as a review of perturbation theory and  how it is applied to relativistic field theories. Here we will use Feynman diagrams and reproduce some of the well known predictions of Standart Model.

detail.LT_SUMA: Sound is a physical phenomenon, while music is a psychological phenomenon. It is amazing how humans have developed a taste for a highly complicated structure of sounds in time-frequency axis and came to call it a ‘music’. Even without lyrics, music has power to touch the human emotion.  This course aims to look into the transition from sound to music, and give students a new perspective to understand music based on physics, physiology, and psychology.
detail.LT_PURO: To understand how a time-series data of air pressure (a.k.a. sound) becomes a music. To understand the physical law governing sound generation and propagation, and the psychological law governing music composing and performance. To understand the linkage between nature and human.

detail.LT_SUMA: Topology, the study of “places” is a basic subject in mathematics, which studies the properties of geometric objects that are preserved by “continuous” deformations. It differs from geometry in the fact that it does not require the ability to measure distances. As topology is needed to understand in detail fundamental concepts like continuity and limits, it is a foundational subjects in modern mathematics, . While in the case of one-dimensional analysis intuition can to large extents be used to guide students to a good level of understanding, in higher dimensions  knowledge of topology is essentially irreplaceable.
detail.LT_PURO: The goal of this course is to introduce students to the basic notions and terminology of the subject so that it naturally fits within the modern language of category theory. Students will also be exposed to some basic aspects of algebraic topology, like the fundamental group and higher homotopy groups.

detail.LT_SUMA: 생체계 내 다양한 물질과 현상은 물리적·역학적 원리를 통해 보다 정량적이고 계량적으로 이해될 수 있다. 생체분자역학개론은 생명과학과 공학의 융합적 관점에서, 세포 내외에서 일어나는 다양한 생명 현상을 유체역학 및 고체역학의 기본 개념을 통해 설명하는 것을 목표로 한다. 예를 들어, 정자(sperm)의 운동을 추진력과 유체 저항의 관점에서 분석하거나, 세포 내 소기관(예: 핵, 미토콘드리아 등)을 세포질이라는 유체 내에 부유된 고체로 간주하고 그 상호작용을 이해하는 식이다. 이와 같은 접근은 생체 분자 및 구조에 대한 기능적 이해를 한층 심화시키는 데 기여할 것이다.
detail.LT_PURO: 본 교과목은 유체 내에서의 drag, 부력, 추진력, 표면장력 등 기본 물리 개념을 생명과학적 맥락에 적용함으로써, 생체 내 복잡한 현상을 직관적이면서도 계량적으로 해석할 수 있는 기반을 제공한다. 또한, 유전체와 단백질 등 생체 고분자를 유체 환경 속의 물질로 바라보고, 구조-기능 간의 관계를 물리적으로 조명하는 다양한 사례를 중심으로 학습할 예정이다. 이를 통해 학생들은 생명과학의 새로운 관점을 경험하고, 공학적 사고를 활용한 생명현상 분석 및 응용 능력을 기르는 것을 목표로 한다.
